figures.finding: Bouvet Island is an uninhabited Norwegian dependency and strict nature reserve with no film or television industry, agreement, fund or incentive; Norway's criminal, private and procedural law apply there, with other Norwegian laws only where they say so (NO).

value.basis: Dependency Act (bilandsloven): Norwegian criminal, private and procedural law apply; other laws only where stated

is an uninhabited subantarctic volcanic island and dependency of Norway . A protected nature reserve situated in the South Atlantic Ocean at the southern end of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge , it is the world's most remote island.
In 1930, following resolution of a dispute with the United Kingdom over claiming rights, it was declared a Norwegian dependency. In 1971, it was designated a nature reserve.
It establishes that Norwegian criminal law , private law and procedural law apply to the island, in addition to other laws that explicitly state they are valid on the island.
